gold_decisions.identity_explanation: ISSUE-004 concerns an invalid replacement of a polynomial norm maximum over a continuous interval when a block spectrum straddles the cluster interval. Gold I001 instead concerns the unestablished existence of a fundamental matrix polynomial, equivalently nonsingularity of the block Vandermonde, despite disjoint block spectra and terminal-matrix assumptions. The predictions therefore identify different mathematical operations and obligations.

ISSUE-007 identifies the false d=2 bound replacing the endpoint-ratio definition of chi_mono by conditioning of B_i, supplies a counterexample, rejects the associated similarity-invariance claim, and gives the corrected eigenvector-conditioning control. This is the same formula and failed similarity-based estimate as gold I002, including its relevant repair.
gold_decisions.shared_mathematical_weakness: Both entries identify that the d=2 display incorrectly controls the endpoint-ratio quantity chi_mono using cond(B_i), whereas similarity through the eigenvector matrices controls the ratio by eigenvector conditioning; the displayed estimate and accompanying similarity-based equality are therefore false.

component_coverage.gold_component: The d=2 chi_mono estimate is falsely expressed in terms of ||B_i|| ||B_i^{-1}|| rather than the endpoint ratios, and the relevant control is eigenvector-matrix conditioning; the associated similarity-invariance equality is also invalid.
component_coverage.recognition_explanation: ISSUE-007 explicitly gives the endpoint-ratio definition, derives its dependence on Omega_j, provides a counterexample where cond(B_j) remains bounded while the ratio grows, rejects the claimed similarity invariance, and specifies the corrected Omega-based estimate.
